subject: URGENT: MedLinkX traffic spikes + decode anomalies after v4.2-q2 rollout
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@medlinkx.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@medlinkx.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Degradations after v4.2-q2 push - urgent

Rishi,

We pushed Redwood model v4.2-q2 to production early this morning per the rollout notes. Since ~08:40 PDT we're seeing:
- p95 latency up from ~240ms to 1.6s, p99 up to ~4.3s
- sustained 5xx error rate increase (mostly 502/503) affecting ~18% of requests
- throughput dropped by ~30% on our hot-path endpoints
- a handful of completions are truncated or produce malformed JSON (see attached request_samples.txt)

This is impacting our clinical routing flows. Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (quant profiles, kernel swaps, or runtime flags) during the window? We need either a rollback or a mitigation ASAP — this is now customer-critical.

Anjali
VP Product, MedLinkX

Attachment: request_samples.txt (text)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@medlinkx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Degradations after v4.2-q2 push - urgent

Anjali — thanks for the signal and the samples. We're seeing matching alarm noise on our side tied to the v4.2-q2 quant profile rollout (automated canary completed at 08:10).

Immediate actions:
1) I am opening INF-4427 and starting an incident bridge now.
2) Requesting an immediate emergency rollback of v4.2-q2 for MedLinkX traffic to v4.1 stable (we'll coordinate a hard pin at the routing level).
3) Evelyn and Marissa are taking lead on root-cause and a hotfix plan — I'll push an exec summary in 30m.

Can we schedule a 30-minute bridge at 10:00 PDT (we'll invite engineering + your on-call)? If that doesn't work, I'll escalate to an exec call at 10:30.

Rishi
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Anjali Rao <anjali@medlinkx.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Quick analysis before bridge — possible KV/cache mismatch

Team / Anjali — quick notes from initial rollup of traces (attached perf_summary.csv):
- Error stack traces show frequent fallback to slow-path attention kernels for the int8 codepath.
- KV-cache hit-rates dropped to ~40% for MedLinkX traffic after rollout; we suspect a serialization mismatch in the qprofile that invalidates prefix caching.
- The combination of more decode re-compute + slow-path kernels would explain both latency and throughput falloff.

Immediate mitigation we can try during the bridge:
- Force traffic for MedLinkX to the v4.1 variant (no quant) — fastest path to relief.
- If rollback timing is constrained, we can apply a runtime flag to force use of the legacy KV encoding for affected shards as a temporary band-aid (non-invasive, reversible).

I attached perf_summary.csv with sample traces.

Marissa
Senior Customer Success Engineer
Attachment: perf_summary.csv (csv)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Anjali Rao <anjali@medlinkx.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Root cause (prelim) + rollback request

On the bridge we reproduced the issue with a replay of MedLinkX hot-path requests. Preliminary findings:
- v4.2-q2 altered quant mapping for several embedding and attention weight groups (int8 packing). That change introduced a byte-ordering difference in the serialized KV cache which makes cached KV entries incompatible across sessions.
- Incompatible KV entries force the runtime to re-materialize prefix states on every request; combined with a kernel selection regression for the int8 scorer this produces significant decode stalls and occasional malformed token sequences when partial state is flushed.

Mitigation plan (recommended):
1) Immediate rollback to v4.1 for MedLinkX traffic (we can complete routing pin in ~6 minutes).
2) Create a hot-patch that restores the previous qprofile mapping and adds a guard that preserves byte-ordering for KV serialization.
3) Post-rollback: run a controlled canary of a corrected qprofile on a small subset of traffic with extended tracing.

I'm requesting exec approval to proceed with the rollback now. This is high-severity; if approved we'll also notify MedLinkX procurement and legal as part of the incident communication plan.

Evelyn
Applied ML, Inference Optimization
Attachment: kv_profile_dump.json (json)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Anjali Rao <anjali@medlinkx.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Exec decision: approve rollback for MedLinkX (v4.2-q2 -> v4.1)

Laura / Aditya — flashing update from the incident bridge: KV cache serialization incompatibility in v4.2-q2 is causing measurable p99 latency spikes and increased 5xxs for MedLinkX. Evelyn proposes rollback + hotfix.

Request: approval to rollback MedLinkX routing to v4.1 immediately. Expected customer relief within 10 minutes and full mitigation within the hour once pins are in place. We'll run post-rollback checks and follow up with a timeline for a corrected qprofile canary.

If approved, I'll notify the customer and CC Legal/Procurement per the incident comms template.

Rishi
